generic.Defined scope/population: All active user accounts on the marketing automation platform and connected martech tools.
generic.In-scope period: The current quarterly martech user access review cycle.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each user row shows role, approval reference, MFA status and last login date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Exported martech user count matches the IAM platform active account count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: User-role export attached to the ITSM access review ticket with export date and reviewer.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every excess or unmatched entitlement is logged with a revoke or approve decision.
generic.Test population: The full active martech user list plus all leaver tickets raised in the quarter.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero unapproved roles and zero enabled martech accounts held by terminated staff.
generic.Exception handling path: Unapproved access is revoked the same day and escalated to the Marketing Manager.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Every user maps to one approved martech role carrying an ITSM approval reference.
generic.Evidence location: ITSM quarterly access review ticket and the martech access matrix in SharePoint.

steps.title: Export the active user-role listing from the marketing automation platform admin console
sop: Open Admin > Users in the marketing automation platform and filter to active accounts.
Export the user, role, MFA and last login columns to the review workbook.
Done when the active user-role export is saved with its extract timestamp.
verify: Check the export row count against the platform active user counter.
Pass when the export matches the platform active user count exactly.

steps.title: Match each martech user to the approved access matrix in SharePoint
sop: Open the approved martech access matrix and join it to the exported user list on user id.
Mark every user whose role is absent from the matrix as an exception.
Record the ITSM approval reference against each matched user.
Done when every exported user carries a matrix decision.
verify: Recount users with no matrix role after the match.
Pass when no active user is left without an approved matrix role.

steps.title: Test segregation of duties on send and compliance-approval permissions in the platform
sop: List users holding campaign-send permission and users holding compliance-approval permission.
Intersect the two lists to expose any user holding both.
Raise a revoke request in ITSM for each conflict found.
Done when the conflict list is empty or fully raised for revocation.
verify: Re-run the intersection after the revocations are applied.
Pass when no marketing user holds both send and compliance-approval rights.

steps.title: Clear the IAM joiner mover leaver queue for martech accounts
sop: Open the IAM platform leaver queue and filter to martech target systems.
Disable every martech account for leaver tickets older than 24 hours.
Record the disable timestamp against each leaver ticket.
Done when no martech leaver ticket is older than 24 hours and still open.
verify: Query the IAM platform for enabled accounts belonging to terminated staff.
Pass when zero terminated employees retain an enabled martech account.

steps.title: Restrict and MFA-enforce martech administrator accounts in the IAM platform
sop: List all admin and superuser accounts in each martech platform.
Remove admin rights from any account not on the named martech administrators list.
Confirm MFA enforcement is active on every remaining admin account.
Done when the admin list matches the named administrators list with MFA on.
verify: Compare the admin account list to the named administrators list and MFA status.
Pass when every admin account is named and MFA enforced.

steps.title: File the access review evidence on the quarterly ITSM review ticket
sop: Attach the user-role export, conflict test result and revocation list to the ITSM ticket.
Record the reviewer name, review date and the exception dispositions.
Close the review ticket once all exceptions carry a disposition.
Done when the quarterly review ticket is closed with evidence attached.
verify: Open the closed ticket and confirm each required attachment is present and dated.
Pass when the review record holds the export, conflict test and dispositions.

generic.Defined scope/population: The validated vendor release for the marketing automation platform production instance.
generic.In-scope period: The approved deployment window recorded on the ITSM change record.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Change record holds sandbox evidence, rollback plan, window and post-release version.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Production platform version equals the version approved in the change record.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Smoke test output and actual start and end times are stored on the change ticket.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every deviation from the plan is noted on the change record with its resolution.
generic.Test population: One test email send, one test form submission and one CRM sync job run.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: All three smoke tests pass and zero campaign sends run inside the window.
generic.Exception handling path: A failed smoke test triggers the documented rollback and a new change record.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: CAB approval, sandbox evidence, rollback plan and post-implementation review recorded.
generic.Evidence location: The ITSM change record for the release plus the platform version history.

steps.title: Confirm the ITSM change record holds sandbox evidence and an approved window
sop: Open the change record and check the attached sandbox validation test results.
Confirm CAB approval, the rollback plan and the agreed deployment window are recorded.
Reject the deployment if any required element is missing.
Done when the change record is complete and approved for the window.
verify: Re-read the change record fields for approval, evidence and rollback plan.
Pass when all four required elements are present and approved.

steps.title: Pause or reschedule campaign sends around the release window
sop: List scheduled sends in the marketing automation platform inside the release window.
Pause or move each send outside the window and confirm with the campaign owner.
Record the paused send ids on the change ticket.
Done when no active send remains scheduled inside the window.
verify: Re-query the platform send schedule for the release window.
Pass when the window contains zero scheduled campaign sends.

steps.title: Apply the vendor release to the production marketing automation platform
sop: Start the deployment at the approved window start time and record the actual start.
Apply the vendor release package to the production instance.
Record the resulting platform version and build number in the change ticket.
Done when the release is applied and the version is recorded.
verify: Compare the production version shown in the platform to the approved version.
Pass when production version matches the version on the change record.

steps.title: Run the post-release smoke test across email, form and CRM sync
sop: Send one test email to the internal seed list and confirm delivery.
Submit one test form and confirm the record is created.
Trigger the CRM sync job and confirm it completes without error.
Done when all three smoke tests have recorded outcomes.
verify: Review the three smoke test outputs attached to the ticket.
Pass when all three smoke tests completed successfully.

steps.title: Resume paused campaign sends in the marketing automation platform
sop: Reinstate each send paused for the window using the recorded send id list.
Confirm scheduled times, audiences and suppression settings are unchanged.
Notify campaign owners that sending has resumed.
Done when every paused send is reinstated and confirmed.
verify: Compare the reinstated send list against the paused send id list.
Pass when every paused send is active again with unchanged settings.

steps.title: Close the ITSM change record with times and deviations
sop: Record actual start and end times against the planned window.
Note any deviation from the plan and the action taken.
Complete the post-implementation review section and close the record.
Done when the change record is closed with the review completed.
verify: Open the closed record and check times, deviations and review section.
Pass when the closed record shows times, deviations and a completed review.

generic.Defined scope/population: All live web forms feeding lead records into the CRM through the marketing platform.
generic.In-scope period: The configuration release covered by the current ITSM change record.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Name, email, consent flag, consent timestamp and source code are non-nullable.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Form submission count equals the CRM lead count for the test window.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Field mapping document and end-to-end test result stored on the change ticket.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Each unrouted or errored lead is logged with its holding queue disposition.
generic.Test population: One end-to-end test lead per live form and channel combination.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Test lead arrives in CRM within the agreed SLA with all tracking fields intact.
generic.Exception handling path: Failed leads land in the integration error queue and alert marketing operations.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Test lead carries source code, campaign id, consent flag and consent timestamp.
generic.Evidence location: ITSM change ticket plus the CRM record of the test lead.

steps.title: Map each web form field to its CRM lead field in the integration configuration
sop: List every live web form field and its target CRM lead field.
Set name, email, consent flag and source code as required and non-nullable.
Record the mapping in the change ticket for review.
Done when every form field has a documented CRM target.
verify: Attempt a submission with a required field blank.
Pass when the submission is rejected and no partial lead is created.

steps.title: Configure consent capture writing to the CRM consent fields
sop: Confirm the consent checkbox value maps to the CRM consent flag field.
Confirm the submission timestamp maps to the CRM consent timestamp field.
Confirm the consent wording version is stored with the record.
Done when consent value, timestamp and wording version all persist.
verify: Inspect the CRM record created by a consented test submission.
Pass when consent flag, timestamp and wording version are all populated.

steps.title: Configure lead assignment rules by product line and territory in the CRM
sop: Build assignment rules keyed on product line and territory.
Set the marketing holding queue as the fallback for unmatched leads.
Activate the rule set and record the version in the change ticket.
Done when the rules are active with a fallback queue configured.
verify: Submit a lead with a territory outside the rule set.
Pass when the unmatched lead lands in the marketing holding queue.

steps.title: Submit an end-to-end test lead through the live form
sop: Complete the live form with test data and a ticked consent box.
Note the submission time and the source and campaign parameters used.
Locate the resulting CRM lead and record its creation time.
Done when the test lead is located in the CRM with its timing recorded.
verify: Compare CRM creation time to submission time and check the field values.
Pass when the lead arrives within SLA with source, campaign and consent intact.

steps.title: Enable the integration error alert to the marketing operations list
sop: Configure the failure alert on the lead integration to the marketing operations list.
Set the alert threshold and the repeat interval.
Trigger a deliberate test failure to fire the alert.
Done when the alert fires and is received by the distribution list.
verify: Confirm receipt of the test alert in the marketing operations inbox.
Pass when the test alert was received with the failing interface named.

steps.title: Clear the integration error queue and close the change ticket
sop: Open the integration error queue and replay or discard the test failures.
Confirm the queue drains to zero after the test run.
Attach the test evidence to the ITSM change ticket and close it.
Done when the queue is empty and the ticket is closed.
verify: Re-query the error queue after the test run.
Pass when no lead record remains stuck in the integration error queue.

generic.Defined scope/population: All martech upgrades and vendor releases planned for the coming release cycle.
generic.In-scope period: The release cycle covered by the published marketing release calendar.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Change ticket names impacted features, window, approvers and communication date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Every impacted integration in the release notes appears in the change ticket.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Release notes, go/no-go record and comms are attached to the change ticket.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Any collision with a campaign send is logged with the reschedule decision.
generic.Test population: All release windows booked in the marketing calendar for the cycle.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero campaign sends scheduled inside an approved release window.
generic.Exception handling path: A collision or missing acknowledgement defers the window to the next slot.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Window booked with named approvers from marketing, IT and CRM recorded.
generic.Evidence location: ITSM change ticket and the marketing release calendar entry.

steps.title: Review the vendor release notes and record impacted martech features
sop: Read the vendor release notes for the platform being upgraded.
List each impacted feature and each impacted integration.
Attach the annotated impact list to the ITSM change ticket.
Done when every impacted feature and integration is listed.
verify: Compare the impact list against the release notes section headings.
Pass when no released change is missing from the impact list.

steps.title: Book the release window in the marketing calendar
sop: Check the marketing calendar for campaign sends and renewal pushes.
Select a window with no send or renewal activity and book it.
Record the booked window on the change ticket.
Done when the window is booked and recorded.
verify: Re-check the calendar and the platform send schedule for the window.
Pass when the window holds no scheduled campaign send or renewal push.

steps.title: Collect acknowledgements from IT, CRM and analytics owners in ITSM
sop: Assign the change ticket to the IT, CRM and analytics owners for review.
Chase any owner who has not acknowledged before the window is confirmed.
Record each acknowledgement with name and date.
Done when all three owners have acknowledged the ticket.
verify: Read the ticket approval log for the three required acknowledgements.
Pass when every required owner acknowledgement is recorded with a date.

steps.title: Publish the release communication to campaign users
sop: Draft the note covering downtime, feature changes and any retraining needed.
Send it to campaign users and agency contacts using the platform.
Record the send date and recipient list on the change ticket.
Done when the communication is sent and recorded.
verify: Check the ticket for the communication attachment and send date.
Pass when the comms record shows content, date and recipient list.

steps.title: Hold the pre-release go or no-go checkpoint
sop: Convene the checkpoint with marketing, IT and CRM representatives.
Review readiness, outstanding risks and the rollback plan.
Record the go or no-go decision and the attendees in the change ticket.
Done when a decision and attendee list are recorded.
verify: Open the change ticket checkpoint section.
Pass when the go or no-go decision names the decider and attendees.

steps.title: Track execution of the release against the booked window
sop: Monitor the release execution against the booked start and end times.
Record any overrun and notify campaign users if downtime extends.
Update the change ticket with the actual execution outcome.
Done when the executed outcome is recorded against the booked window.
verify: Compare actual execution times to the booked window on the ticket.
Pass when execution is recorded with any overrun explained.

generic.Defined scope/population: Customer records across CRM, policy admin and the warehouse subject to identity matching.
generic.In-scope period: The rule version being approved and its stated effective date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each match key has a confidence threshold and each attribute has a survivorship source.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Golden record count plus unmatched count equals the input source record count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Rule set version, test results and approval date published to the data catalog.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Records failing all match keys are logged as unresolved with a review decision.
generic.Test population: The labelled sample of known matched and known distinct customer pairs.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: False-merge and false-split rates stay inside the agreed tolerance.
generic.Exception handling path: Pairs above threshold but below auto-merge go to manual stewardship review.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Match keys, thresholds and survivorship rules are configured, approved and dated.
generic.Evidence location: Data catalog entry for the customer master and the rule test result set.

steps.title: Document the match key hierarchy in the data catalog
sop: List match keys in priority order: policy number, then email plus surname, then postal address.
Record the confidence threshold applied to each key.
Publish the hierarchy to the customer master catalog entry.
Done when every match key has a documented priority and threshold.
verify: Read back the catalog entry for the key hierarchy.
Pass when each key shows a priority position and a confidence threshold.

steps.title: Define survivorship rules per attribute across CRM and policy admin
sop: For each customer attribute name the winning source system.
Set policy admin as the source for legal name and CRM for contact preferences.
Record the rule and its rationale in the catalog entry.
Done when every attribute has one named winning source.
verify: Check the attribute list for any attribute with no winning source.
Pass when no attribute is left without a survivorship rule.

steps.title: Run the rule set over the labelled sample in the warehouse
sop: Load the labelled sample of known matched and distinct pairs.
Execute the rule set and capture the merge decision per pair.
Calculate the false-merge and false-split rates.
Done when both error rates are calculated and recorded.
verify: Compare the measured rates against the agreed tolerance.
Pass when false-merge and false-split rates are inside tolerance.

steps.title: Confirm golden records retain source record cross-references
sop: Inspect the golden record table for the contributing source id array.
Confirm every contributing source record id is retained on merge.
Fix the merge job if any contributing id is dropped.
Done when all merged records carry their full source id set.
verify: Query golden records with an empty source cross-reference.
Pass when no golden record exists without a source-record cross-reference.

steps.title: Review the rule set with marketing and insights stakeholders
sop: Walk the match keys, thresholds and survivorship rules with marketing users.
Capture objections where a rule would break a targeting use case.
Adjust thresholds where the review agrees a change is needed.
Done when stakeholder comments are captured and dispositioned.
verify: Read the review record for open unresolved comments.
Pass when every stakeholder comment carries a disposition.

steps.title: Publish and activate the approved rule set with a review date
sop: Approve the rule version and record the approver name and date.
Activate the rules in the warehouse identity resolution job.
Set the next review date on the catalog entry.
Done when the rules are active and the review date is set.
verify: Confirm the active rule version matches the approved version in the catalog.
Pass when the active version, approver and next review date all agree.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every marketing dataset registered in the data catalog across the warehouse.
generic.In-scope period: The current stewardship assignment review cycle.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each dataset shows a named business owner, technical steward and acknowledgement date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Catalog dataset count matches the count of stewardship assignments recorded.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Published stewardship matrix carries its version and publication date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Unacknowledged or vacant stewardships are logged with a reassignment decision.
generic.Test population: All marketing datasets listed in the catalog at the review cut-off date.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero marketing datasets without both an owner and a steward.
generic.Exception handling path: A leaver steward triggers reassignment with an effective date logged.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Every dataset has an owner and steward with a recorded acknowledgement date.
generic.Evidence location: Data catalog stewardship fields and the governance site stewardship matrix.

steps.title: List every marketing dataset and its stewardship fields in the data catalog
sop: Filter the catalog to marketing domain datasets.
Export dataset name, business owner, technical steward and acknowledgement date.
Flag rows with a blank owner or steward.
Done when the full dataset list with stewardship fields is exported.
verify: Count exported datasets against the catalog marketing domain total.
Pass when the export covers every marketing dataset in the catalog.

steps.title: Confirm steward approval rights on schema and access changes
sop: Open the catalog permission settings for each marketing dataset.
Confirm the named steward holds schema and access change approval rights.
Correct any dataset where the rights sit elsewhere.
Done when every steward holds the approval rights for their dataset.
verify: Re-check the permission settings after correction.
Pass when each steward holds approval rights on their own dataset.

steps.title: Chase and record acknowledgements from unconfirmed stewards
sop: Identify stewards with no acknowledgement recorded.
Send the assignment note and request confirmation.
Record the acknowledgement date on the catalog entry when received.
Done when every steward has acknowledged or been escalated.
verify: Query catalog entries with a blank acknowledgement date.
Pass when each steward assignment carries an acknowledgement date.

steps.title: Reassign stewardship for datasets whose steward has left
sop: Cross-check steward names against the active employee directory.
Reassign datasets whose steward has left to a current named steward.
Log the change with its effective date in the catalog.
Done when no dataset is assigned to a leaver.
verify: Rerun the directory cross-check on the steward list.
Pass when every named steward is an active employee.

steps.title: Enforce stewardship in the IAM platform access request workflow
sop: Confirm the IAM access request for each dataset routes to its named steward.
Correct routing rules pointing at a shared mailbox or a leaver.
Record the routing configuration reviewed and the date.
Done when every dataset request routes to its named steward.
verify: Raise a test access request against one marketing dataset.
Pass when the request routes to the named steward for approval.

steps.title: Publish the marketing stewardship matrix to the governance site
sop: Assemble the current dataset, owner, steward and acknowledgement date list.
Publish it to the shared governance site with a version number.
Notify marketing and compliance that the matrix is updated.
Done when the matrix is published and notified.
verify: Open the published matrix and compare it to the catalog export.
Pass when the published matrix matches the catalog for every dataset.

generic.Defined scope/population: The martech access matrix and its supporting governance document set.
generic.In-scope period: All access, role and platform changes made since the last document revision.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Front page shows version number, author, effective date and next review date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Documented platform and role list matches the live martech access matrix.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Latest completed quarterly access review is attached to the document set.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Any approval path mismatch is logged with the correction made.
generic.Test population: Every martech platform named in the governance document set.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero uncontrolled draft copies present in the published folder.
generic.Exception handling path: A documented path that differs from the live workflow is corrected before publication.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Current version published with owner, version number and next review date.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint governance library and the compliance evidence repository copy.

steps.title: Update the martech access matrix for changes since the last revision
sop: List role, platform and permission changes made since the last revision date.
Amend the access matrix rows to reflect each change.
Record the change summary on the revision history page.
Done when every logged change is reflected in the matrix.
verify: Compare the matrix against the current platform role listing.
Pass when the documented roles match the live platform roles.

steps.title: Test the documented approval path against the live IAM request workflow
sop: For each platform read the documented approval path.
Raise or inspect a request in the IAM platform to see the enforced path.
Correct the document where the enforced path differs.
Done when documented and enforced paths agree for every platform.
verify: Re-inspect one request per platform after correction.
Pass when each platform enforces exactly the documented approval path.

steps.title: Attach the latest quarterly access review as evidence
sop: Retrieve the most recently completed quarterly user access review record.
Attach it to the governance document set in the evidence repository.
Record the review period covered by the attachment.
Done when the current review evidence is attached and dated.
verify: Check the attached review period against the current quarter.
Pass when the attached access review covers the most recent completed cycle.

steps.title: Stamp version, author and effective date and supersede the prior version
sop: Increment the version number on the front page.
Record author, effective date and next review date.
Mark the prior version superseded and move it to the archive folder.
Done when the new version is stamped and the prior one is archived.
verify: List the published folder contents for older versions.
Pass when only the current version is present in the published folder.

steps.title: Restrict edit rights on the SharePoint document library
sop: Open the library permission settings in SharePoint.
Limit edit rights to the named martech administrators group.
Set read access for the wider marketing audience.
Done when edit rights are limited to the administrators group.
verify: Attempt an edit with a standard marketing account.
Pass when a non-administrator account cannot edit the published document.

steps.title: Publish the governance document set and remove uncontrolled copies
sop: Publish the updated set to the SharePoint governance library.
Search the library for working drafts and duplicate copies.
Delete or archive any uncontrolled copy found.
Done when only controlled copies remain published.
verify: Search the published folder for draft or copy filenames.
Pass when no uncontrolled draft copy of the access matrix is present.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every martech application in use across marketing and its supporting vendor contract.
generic.In-scope period: The current inventory review cycle up to the stated review cut-off date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each entry shows vendor, contract end date, annual cost, owner and personal-data flag.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Inventory entry count matches the active marketing contract count in the repository.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Inventory version, review date and circulation record stored in SharePoint.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Platforms without a contract or risk assessment are flagged with an owner action.
generic.Test population: All active marketing vendor contracts in the contract repository.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero active marketing contracts missing from the martech stack inventory.
generic.Exception handling path: An unlisted platform is added and routed for vendor risk assessment.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each entry shows owner, contract end date, cost and personal-data indicator.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint martech inventory workbook and the contract lifecycle repository.

steps.title: Refresh the inventory entries from the ITSM application register
sop: Export marketing applications from the ITSM application register.
Add any application in use but missing from the inventory workbook.
Populate vendor, contract end date, annual cost and business owner per entry.
Done when every application in use has a complete inventory row.
verify: Count inventory rows with any mandatory field blank.
Pass when no inventory entry is missing a mandatory field.

steps.title: Cross-check the inventory against the contract lifecycle repository
sop: Export active marketing contracts from the contract repository.
Join the contract list to the inventory on vendor and platform name.
Add an inventory entry for every contract with no match.
Done when every active contract maps to an inventory entry.
verify: Re-run the join after the additions.
Pass when no active marketing vendor contract is missing from the inventory.

steps.title: Record integration points and the personal-data indicator per platform
sop: For each platform list its integrations to CRM, warehouse and web.
Set the personal-data indicator where the platform processes personal data.
Record the data classification alongside the indicator.
Done when every entry shows integrations and a personal-data indicator.
verify: Filter the inventory for blank integration or indicator fields.
Pass when every platform entry carries integrations and the indicator.

steps.title: Flag platforms lacking a contract or a vendor risk assessment
sop: Compare each platform to the contract and risk assessment records.
Flag platforms with no active contract or no completed risk assessment.
Raise an ITSM action for each flagged platform with an owner.
Done when every flagged platform has a raised action.
verify: List flagged platforms without an ITSM action reference.
Pass when every flagged platform carries an action and an owner.

steps.title: Set the next review date and version the inventory
sop: Record the review date, reviewer and inventory version in the workbook.
Set the next review date per the agreed cadence.
Archive the prior version in SharePoint.
Done when the version and next review date are recorded.
verify: Open the workbook header fields.
Pass when version, reviewer, review date and next review date are all set.

steps.title: Circulate the updated inventory to leadership and procurement
sop: Share the published inventory link with marketing leadership and procurement.
Highlight platforms flagged for missing contract or risk assessment.
Record the circulation date and recipients.
Done when the inventory is circulated and recorded.
verify: Check the circulation record against the approved recipient list.
Pass when the circulation record shows date and full recipient list.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every data flow linking web forms, campaign platform, CRM, warehouse and activation tools.
generic.In-scope period: The current flow map revision covering interfaces live at the cut-off date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each flow records source, target, method, frequency, volume and data classification.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Mapped interface count matches the interface list held in the data catalog lineage.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Flow map version and author are stored with the catalog lineage snapshot.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Flows with no lawful basis recorded are logged and routed to compliance.
generic.Test population: All marketing datasets and the interfaces feeding them for the period.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Every personal-data flow shows a classification and a lawful basis.
generic.Exception handling path: An undocumented external transfer is stopped until a contract clause is confirmed.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Lineage for each marketing dataset resolves to a documented upstream source.
generic.Evidence location: Data catalog lineage entries and the published martech flow map.

steps.title: Draw each hop from web form and campaign platform into the warehouse
sop: List the interfaces from web forms and the campaign platform into the CRM.
Extend each chain through the warehouse and out to activation platforms.
Draw the hops in the flow map with source and target named.
Done when every known interface appears as a drawn hop.
verify: Compare the drawn hops against the integration inventory.
Pass when every inventory interface appears on the flow map.

steps.title: Label personal-data flows with classification and lawful basis
sop: Mark each flow carrying personal data on the map.
Record the data classification for each marked flow.
Record the lawful basis or the consent source behind each flow.
Done when every personal-data flow carries classification and basis.
verify: Filter the map for personal-data flows with a blank basis.
Pass when no personal-data flow lacks a classification and legal basis.

steps.title: Record transfer method, frequency and volume per interface
sop: For each interface record the transfer method and protocol.
Record the run frequency and the typical record volume per run.
Add the values to the flow map annotation table.
Done when each interface shows method, frequency and volume.
verify: List interfaces missing any of the three attributes.
Pass when every mapped interface records method, frequency and volume.

steps.title: Flag external vendor flows and confirm contract cover
sop: Identify flows sending marketing data outside the company.
Check the contract repository for a clause covering each transfer.
Flag any transfer without a covering clause for immediate review.
Done when every external flow has a contract position recorded.
verify: List external flows with no contract clause reference.
Pass when every external marketing data flow cites a contract clause.

steps.title: Reconcile the drawn map against catalog lineage
sop: Export the lineage held in the data catalog for marketing datasets.
Compare it against the drawn flow map hop by hop.
Resolve each discrepancy by correcting the map or the lineage.
Done when map and catalog lineage agree.
verify: Re-run the comparison after corrections.
Pass when lineage for each marketing dataset resolves to a documented source.

steps.title: Publish the flow map and set its review date
sop: Publish the flow map version to the data catalog and shared library.
Record author, version and publication date.
Set the next review date and notify the stewards.
Done when the map is published with a review date set.
verify: Open the published map header fields.
Pass when version, author, date and next review date are all recorded.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every martech platform and integration endpoint listed in the stack inventory.
generic.In-scope period: The current reporting month for availability measurement.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each platform shows measured availability, contracted SLA and variance.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Monitored platform count equals the platform count in the martech inventory.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Monthly uptime summary published with its generation date on the dashboard.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every outage above threshold has an ITSM incident with a closure disposition.
generic.Test population: All outages recorded against martech platforms during the month.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Measured availability meets the contracted SLA for each platform.
generic.Exception handling path: An SLA breach is raised with the vendor and tracked to service credit or fix.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Current month availability is published for every platform in the inventory.
generic.Evidence location: ITSM incident records and the marketing operations uptime dashboard.

steps.title: Enable uptime monitoring on every martech platform and endpoint
sop: Take the platform and endpoint list from the martech stack inventory.
Confirm a monitor exists for each platform and each integration endpoint.
Create monitors for anything unmonitored.
Done when every inventory item has an active monitor.
verify: Compare the monitor list to the inventory list.
Pass when every inventory platform and endpoint has an active monitor.

steps.title: Confirm vendor status page subscriptions route to marketing operations
sop: List the vendor status pages for each martech platform.
Confirm an active subscription routed to the marketing operations inbox.
Subscribe where missing and send a test notification.
Done when every vendor status feed reaches the operations inbox.
verify: Check the operations inbox for each vendor test notification.
Pass when a status notification was received for every platform.

steps.title: Measure monthly availability against contracted SLA
sop: Extract measured availability per platform for the month from the monitor.
Compare it to the contracted SLA figure for that platform.
Record the variance in the uptime workbook.
Done when every platform has a measured and contracted figure recorded.
verify: List platforms with a missing availability or SLA figure.
Pass when every platform shows measured availability and its SLA variance.

steps.title: Raise ITSM incidents for outages above the alert threshold
sop: List outages that exceeded the alert threshold during the month.
Raise an ITSM incident for each with start time, end time and duration.
Record the campaign impact on each incident.
Done when every qualifying outage carries an incident record.
verify: Join the outage list to the incident list for the month.
Pass when each outage above threshold has an incident with duration and impact.

steps.title: Publish the monthly uptime summary to the operations dashboard
sop: Build the summary showing availability, SLA and incident count per platform.
Publish it to the marketing operations dashboard in the BI platform.
Record the generation date and data cut-off on the page.
Done when the summary is published with its cut-off date.
verify: Open the dashboard page and check platform coverage.
Pass when current month availability is published for every inventory platform.

steps.title: Review SLA breaches with the vendor and record the outcome
sop: Take each SLA breach to the vendor service review.
Request the service credit or remediation commitment due.
Record the vendor response and the agreed action in the incident.
Done when every breach has a recorded vendor outcome.
verify: Read the incidents raised for SLA breaches this month.
Pass when each breach shows a vendor response and agreed action.

generic.Defined scope/population: All licensed martech seats and contracted volume tiers across marketing platforms.
generic.In-scope period: The current reconciliation period ahead of the platform renewal date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each platform row shows active seats, entitlement, dormant seats and invoice value.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Active seat count reconciles to the contracted entitlement per platform.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Seat exports and the reconciliation workbook are saved with extract dates.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every dormant or excess seat is logged with a reclaim or exception decision.
generic.Test population: All licensed accounts and contracted volume tiers for the period.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Active seats at or below entitlement and no unexplained 90 day dormancy.
generic.Exception handling path: Overage exposure is raised to the vendor and to the budget holder before renewal.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Active seat count is at or below the contracted entitlement for each platform.
generic.Evidence location: Reconciliation workbook plus the contract repository entitlement record.

steps.title: Export active seat counts from each martech platform
sop: Export the active account list from each martech platform admin console.
Record the seat count and extract timestamp per platform.
Load the counts into the reconciliation workbook.
Done when every platform has a dated seat count recorded.
verify: Compare workbook counts to the platform admin counters.
Pass when each recorded seat count matches its platform counter.

steps.title: Compare seat counts to contracted entitlement in the contract repository
sop: Retrieve the contracted entitlement for each platform from the repository.
Compare active seats to entitlement and calculate the difference.
Flag every platform above entitlement.
Done when every platform shows a seats-versus-entitlement position.
verify: List platforms with active seats above entitlement.
Pass when active seat count is at or below entitlement for every platform.

steps.title: Identify dormant accounts with no login in 90 days
sop: Filter the seat export for accounts with no login in the last 90 days.
Confirm with the line manager whether each account is still needed.
Mark accounts for reclaim or downgrade and record any exception.
Done when every dormant account has a decision recorded.
verify: List dormant accounts with no recorded decision.
Pass when no dormant account is left without a decision or exception.

steps.title: Compare contracted volume tiers to actual record counts
sop: Retrieve the contracted contact or database volume tier per platform.
Extract the actual record count held in each platform.
Flag any platform approaching or exceeding its tier.
Done when every platform tier position is recorded.
verify: Check flagged platforms against the tier thresholds.
Pass when every overage exposure is quantified and flagged.

steps.title: Reconcile platform invoices to entitlement in the ledger
sop: Extract the platform invoice lines posted in the ledger for the period.
Match each line to the entitlement and contracted rate.
Raise a vendor query for any mismatch and record the reference.
Done when every invoice line is matched or queried.
verify: List invoice lines with no match and no query reference.
Pass when every invoice line is matched or carries a vendor query.

steps.title: Record reclaimed seats and the cost impact for renewal
sop: Total the reclaimed and downgraded seats across platforms.
Calculate the resulting cost impact at the contracted rate.
Record the position in the renewal preparation note.
Done when the reclaim total and cost impact are recorded.
verify: Check the renewal note against the reclaim decisions logged.
Pass when reclaimed seat count and cost impact agree with the decisions.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every platform in the martech stack inventory with its cost and utilisation data.
generic.In-scope period: The reporting period covered by the closed general ledger.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each platform shows spend, active users, sends, records and cost per active user.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Reported martech spend ties to the general ledger balance for the period.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Issued report filed in SharePoint with issue date and version number.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Low-utilisation platforms are logged as rationalisation candidates with an owner.
generic.Test population: All martech cost centre postings and platform utilisation extracts for the period.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Reported spend agrees to the ledger with zero unexplained difference.
generic.Exception handling path: An unreconciled ledger difference is investigated before the report is issued.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Report shows cost, utilisation and cost per active user for every platform.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint report library and the BI martech cost and usage dataset.

steps.title: Pull period martech spend by cost centre from the general ledger
sop: Extract postings for the martech cost centres from the closed ledger.
Reconcile the extract to the invoice register for the period.
Record the reconciled spend by platform.
Done when platform spend is extracted and reconciled.
verify: Compare the extract total to the ledger cost centre balance.
Pass when reported spend ties to the general ledger for the period.

steps.title: Assemble per-platform utilisation metrics
sop: Extract active users, send volume and record counts per platform.
Align the utilisation period to the ledger reporting period.
Load the metrics beside the spend figures.
Done when every platform has utilisation data for the period.
verify: List platforms with missing utilisation metrics.
Pass when every inventory platform carries utilisation for the period.

steps.title: Calculate cost per active user and total cost of ownership
sop: Divide platform spend by active users to give cost per active user.
Add licence, implementation and vendor support lines for total cost of ownership.
Record both measures per platform in the BI dataset.
Done when both measures exist for every platform.
verify: Check the calculation on two sampled platforms.
Pass when both sampled figures recompute from the underlying data.

steps.title: Highlight low-utilisation rationalisation candidates
sop: Compare each platform utilisation against the agreed threshold.
Flag platforms below the threshold as rationalisation candidates.
Record the contract end date and notice period for each candidate.
Done when every below-threshold platform is flagged with contract dates.
verify: Read the candidate list against the utilisation figures.
Pass when every below-threshold platform is flagged as a candidate.

steps.title: Build and review the martech performance and cost report
sop: Assemble the report covering spend, utilisation, cost per user and candidates.
Review the narrative against the underlying figures.
Correct any inconsistency before issue.
Done when the report is reviewed and ready to issue.
verify: Spot check three report figures against the BI dataset.
Pass when all three sampled figures match the source dataset.

steps.title: Issue the report to the CMO and finance and file the copy
sop: Receive and review the issued martech cost and performance report.
Record decisions on any rationalisation candidate raised.
Confirm the published copy is filed in SharePoint with its issue date.
Done when the report is issued, decided and filed.
verify: Open the filed copy and check issue date and recipient list.
Pass when the filed report shows issue date, recipients and decisions.

generic.Defined scope/population: All failed records sitting in the martech to CRM integration error queue.
generic.In-scope period: The failure window from first error to queue drain confirmation.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each incident records interface, error code, affected record count and root cause.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Replayed record count equals the failed record count captured at the start.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Error queue export and replay log are attached to the ITSM incident.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Records that cannot be replayed are quarantined with a documented disposition.
generic.Test population: Every record in the error queue plus the consent and opt-out subset.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Error queue drains to zero with no consent record overwritten.
generic.Exception handling path: Unreplayable records are escalated to the Data Analyst for manual correction.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Incident records root cause, affected record count and preventive action.
generic.Evidence location: ITSM incident record and the integration platform replay log.

steps.title: Export the integration error queue and classify the failures
sop: Open the integration error queue in the marketing automation platform.
Export failing interface, error code and record identifiers.
Count the affected records per error code.
Done when the failure classification and counts are recorded.
verify: Compare the exported count to the queue depth counter.
Pass when the export count equals the reported queue depth.

steps.title: Quarantine failed consent and opt-out records for controlled replay
sop: Filter the failed records for lead, consent and opt-out payloads.
Move the consent and opt-out records into the quarantine table.
Record the quarantined count and the reason.
Done when consent and opt-out failures are quarantined and counted.
verify: Compare quarantine table counts to the filtered failure counts.
Pass when every consent or opt-out failure is present in quarantine.

steps.title: Apply the fix to the failing interface
sop: Diagnose whether the cause is credential, mapping or payload related.
Apply the corrective configuration change to the interface.
Record the change on the ITSM incident.
Done when the fix is applied and recorded.
verify: Push one test record through the fixed interface.
Pass when the test record syncs without error.

steps.title: Replay the failed records and drain the queue
sop: Replay the failed records in the order captured.
Monitor the queue depth as the replay progresses.
Log any record that fails a second time.
Done when the queue depth reaches zero or residual failures are logged.
verify: Re-read the error queue depth after the replay.
Pass when no unresolved integration errors remain after replay.

steps.title: Verify replayed preferences did not overwrite newer values in the CRM
sop: Compare the replayed consent and opt-out timestamps to the CRM current values.
Identify any case where an older preference overwrote a newer one.
Restore the newer preference and record the correction.
Done when no stale preference remains applied.
verify: Query the CRM for consent records older than their source timestamp.
Pass when no replayed record overwrote a more recent preference.

steps.title: Record root cause and preventive action and close the incident
sop: Write the root cause statement on the ITSM incident.
Record the preventive action and its owner and due date.
Attach the queue export and replay log and close the incident.
Done when the incident is closed with cause and prevention recorded.
verify: Open the closed incident and check the required fields.
Pass when root cause, record count and preventive action are all recorded.

generic.Defined scope/population: The vendor release applied to the martech sandbox ahead of production.
generic.In-scope period: The sandbox validation window recorded on the ITSM change record.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each regression case shows a result, tester name and execution date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Executed regression case count matches the approved regression script case count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Signed test results attached to the change record with the release version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Each defect found is logged with severity and an open or closed disposition.
generic.Test population: The full regression script covering send, landing page, form, segmentation and sync.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: All regression cases pass and no severity 1 or 2 defect remains open.
generic.Exception handling path: A severity 1 or 2 defect blocks promotion until fixed and retested.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: All regression cases including unsubscribe handling are marked passed.
generic.Evidence location: ITSM change record sandbox evidence attachment and the test result set.

steps.title: Refresh the sandbox to match production configuration
sop: Trigger the sandbox refresh from the production configuration.
Confirm templates, lists and integration settings match production.
Record the refresh completion time on the change record.
Done when the sandbox mirrors production configuration.
verify: Compare key configuration settings between sandbox and production.
Pass when sampled settings match between the two environments.

steps.title: Apply the vendor release to the sandbox instance
sop: Apply the vendor release package to the sandbox.
Record the resulting version and build number.
Confirm the sandbox version matches the release under test.
Done when the release is applied and the version recorded.
verify: Read the sandbox version against the release notes version.
Pass when the sandbox runs exactly the release under test.

steps.title: Execute the regression script across send, page, form and segmentation
sop: Execute each regression case in the approved script.
Record pass or fail with evidence per case.
Re-run any case with an ambiguous result.
Done when every regression case has a recorded result.
verify: Count cases executed against the script case list.
Pass when every scripted regression case has a recorded outcome.

steps.title: Test suppression list and unsubscribe handling in the sandbox
sop: Add a test contact to the suppression list and attempt a send.
Submit an unsubscribe from a test email and confirm the flag is set.
Confirm the suppressed contact receives no message.
Done when suppression and unsubscribe behaviour is confirmed.
verify: Check the send log for delivery to the suppressed contact.
Pass when the suppressed contact received nothing and the opt-out persisted.

steps.title: Log defects with severity and confirm the blocking position
sop: Log every defect found with its severity and reproduction steps.
Confirm no severity 1 or 2 defect remains open.
Escalate to the vendor where a blocking defect is theirs.
Done when the defect list is complete and severities assigned.
verify: Filter the defect list for open severity 1 and 2 items.
Pass when no open severity 1 or 2 defect is recorded against the release.

steps.title: Attach the signed test results to the change record
sop: Assemble the regression results, defect list and CRM sync evidence.
Sign the result set with tester name and date.
Attach it to the change record as sandbox validation evidence.
Done when the signed evidence is attached to the change record.
verify: Open the change record attachments.
Pass when signed sandbox validation evidence is present and dated.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every audience segment intended for outbound contact on any marketing channel.
generic.In-scope period: The consent snapshot date applied to the segment before its send.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each member has a consent flag, consent source and consent timestamp per channel.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Segment count plus suppressed count equals the pre-suppression population.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Segment definition notes record the consent snapshot date and rules applied.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Records removed by suppression are logged with the rule that removed them.
generic.Test population: All members of the finished segment plus the global suppression list.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero opted-out or do-not-contact records remain in the segment.
generic.Exception handling path: Any opted-out record found is removed and the segment build is re-run.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each member has a consent record with source and timestamp for the channel.
generic.Evidence location: Segment definition notes in the marketing platform and the warehouse snapshot.

steps.title: Filter each segment query on the channel consent flag
sop: Open the segment query in the warehouse and identify the intended channel.
Add the consent flag filter for that channel to the query.
Re-run the query and record the resulting count.
Done when every segment query filters on its channel consent flag.
verify: Inspect the query text for the channel consent predicate.
Pass when each segment query filters on the correct channel consent flag.

steps.title: Apply the global suppression and do-not-contact lists
sop: Join the segment against the global suppression list.
Join it against the do-not-contact list for the channel.
Remove matches and record the suppressed count.
Done when both lists are applied and counts recorded.
verify: Re-join the finished segment against both lists.
Pass when no contact with an active opt-out or do-not-contact flag remains.

steps.title: Remove records whose opt-out date is later than their consent date
sop: Compare consent date and opt-out date on each remaining member.
Remove any record whose opt-out post-dates its consent.
Record the removed count and reason.
Done when no later opt-out remains in the segment.
verify: Query the segment for members with opt-out later than consent.
Pass when the query returns zero rows.

steps.title: Exclude restricted and deceased flagged records
sop: Join the segment to the data-use restriction and deceased flags in the CRM.
Remove every flagged record from the segment.
Record the excluded count by flag type.
Done when all flagged records are excluded.
verify: Re-join the segment to the restriction and deceased flags.
Pass when no restricted or deceased record remains in the segment.

steps.title: Reconcile the segment counts before and after suppression
sop: Record the pre-suppression population count.
Record the suppressed count by rule and the final segment count.
Confirm the three figures reconcile.
Done when the counts reconcile without residual.
verify: Add final count and suppressed count and compare to the population.
Pass when segment plus suppressed equals the pre-suppression population.

steps.title: Record the consent snapshot date and rules in the segment notes
sop: Write the consent snapshot date into the segment definition notes.
List the suppression rules applied and the counts removed.
Record the approver and the date of approval.
Done when the notes carry snapshot date, rules and approval.
verify: Open the segment definition notes in the marketing platform.
Pass when snapshot date, applied rules and approver are all recorded.

generic.Defined scope/population: Marketing records and audit trails reaching their retention trigger this period.
generic.In-scope period: The archive run window covering records at or past their retention trigger.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each archive batch records batch id, record counts, retention rule and disposal date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Archived record count equals the identified in-scope record count for the run.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Archive manifest and retrieval test result stored with their run timestamps.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Records held back from the run are logged with the legal hold reference.
generic.Test population: The sampled archived items selected for the retrieval test.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Sampled retrieval completes inside the agreed retrieval SLA.
generic.Exception handling path: A failed retrieval halts disposal until the archive package is repaired.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Archived campaign package holds creative, approvals, audience snapshot and send log.
generic.Evidence location: Compliance evidence repository archive record and the retention log.

steps.title: Identify records reaching their retention trigger this period
sop: Run the retention report over marketing records in the warehouse.
Confirm the applicable retention period for each record type.
List the in-scope records with their trigger dates.
Done when the in-scope population is listed and counted.
verify: Compare the listed population to the retention rule criteria.
Pass when every listed record meets its stated retention trigger.

steps.title: Assemble the campaign archive package
sop: Gather creative materials, approval evidence, audience snapshot and send log per campaign.
Bundle them into a single archive package per campaign id.
Record the package contents in the manifest.
Done when each campaign has a complete archive package.
verify: Open a sampled package and check for the four required components.
Pass when the sampled package holds creative, approvals, snapshot and send log.

steps.title: Exclude records under legal hold from the run
sop: Retrieve the current legal hold list from the compliance repository.
Remove every held record from the archive-and-purge manifest.
Record the excluded record references and the hold reference.
Done when no held record remains on the manifest.
verify: Join the purge manifest against the legal hold list.
Pass when no record subject to legal hold appears in the purge manifest.

steps.title: Write the archive batch to the evidence repository
sop: Write the packages to the compliance evidence repository archive store.
Record the batch id, record counts and write timestamp.
Confirm the written count matches the manifest count.
Done when the batch is written and counts reconcile.
verify: Compare the written record count to the manifest count.
Pass when the archived count equals the in-scope record count.

steps.title: Run the retrieval test on a sample of archived items
sop: Select the agreed sample of archived items.
Retrieve each item and record the elapsed retrieval time.
Confirm the retrieved content is complete and readable.
Done when every sampled item is retrieved and timed.
verify: Compare the elapsed retrieval times against the SLA.
Pass when every sampled retrieval completed inside the SLA.

steps.title: Record the batch and disposal date in the retention log
sop: Record the batch id, record counts and retention rule in the retention log.
Record the scheduled disposal date for the batch.
Attach the retrieval test evidence to the log entry.
Done when the retention log entry is complete.
verify: Open the retention log entry for the batch.
Pass when batch id, counts, disposal date and test evidence are recorded.

generic.Defined scope/population: Prospect and customer marketing contact records in the CRM and warehouse.
generic.In-scope period: The current cleanse and deduplication run window.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Name, address and email are standardised to the agreed reference format.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Input record count equals surviving records plus merged plus quarantined records.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Before and after quality scores published with the run date to the dashboard.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Quarantined records are logged with the validation rule that failed.
generic.Test population: The active marketing contact set after the merge run completes.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero exact-email duplicate pairs remain in the active contact set.
generic.Exception handling path: Match candidates below the auto-merge threshold go to manual review.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Surviving record retains earliest consent date and latest opt-out date.
generic.Evidence location: Data quality dashboard run record and the merge audit table.

steps.title: Standardise name, address and email formats in the warehouse
sop: Apply the agreed reference formatting rules to name, address and email.
Record the count of records changed by each rule.
Write the standardised values into the staging table.
Done when all three attribute types are standardised and counted.
verify: Sample twenty standardised records against the reference rules.
Pass when every sampled record matches the reference format.

steps.title: Run duplicate detection and review match candidates
sop: Run the duplicate detection rule set over the standardised records.
Split candidates into auto-merge and manual review by threshold.
Review the manual candidates and confirm or reject each merge.
Done when every candidate has a merge decision.
verify: List candidates with no recorded merge decision.
Pass when no match candidate is left without a decision.

steps.title: Apply merges preserving consent and opt-out dates
sop: Merge confirmed duplicates into the surviving record.
Carry the earliest consent date onto the survivor.
Carry the most recent opt-out date onto the survivor.
Done when every merge preserves both date rules.
verify: Query survivors whose consent date is later than a merged source.
Pass when survivors retain earliest consent and latest opt-out dates.

steps.title: Quarantine records failing email or address validation
sop: Apply email and address validation rules to the remaining records.
Move failing records into the quarantine table rather than deleting them.
Record the failing rule and the quarantine count.
Done when all failures are quarantined and counted.
verify: Check the quarantine table for records without a failure reason.
Pass when every quarantined record carries its failing rule.

steps.title: Reconcile input, surviving, merged and quarantined counts
sop: Record the input record count for the run.
Record surviving, merged and quarantined counts.
Confirm the three outputs sum to the input count.
Done when the counts reconcile without residual.
verify: Add the output counts and compare to the input count.
Pass when the totals reconcile exactly.

steps.title: Publish before and after quality scores to the dashboard
sop: Calculate duplicate rate and completeness before and after the run.
Publish both to the data quality dashboard with the run date.
Notify the marketing stewards of the change.
Done when the scores are published with the run date.
verify: Open the dashboard and re-check the exact-email duplicate rate.
Pass when no exact-email duplicate pair remains in the active set.

generic.Defined scope/population: Sends, opens, clicks, form submissions and unsubscribes from the marketing platform.
generic.In-scope period: The incremental load window defined by the watermark column.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each engagement row carries event type, contact key, event timestamp and campaign id.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Landing table row counts reconcile to the platform API counts for the test window.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Catalog registration and load run log record owner, schedule and run timestamps.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Late-arriving and rejected rows are logged with their handling decision.
generic.Test population: One agreed test window replayed twice through the ingestion pipeline.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero duplicate engagement rows after a deliberate re-run of the window.
generic.Exception handling path: A load failure alerts marketing analytics and the window is re-run idempotently.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Row counts for the test window reconcile to the platform source counts.
generic.Evidence location: Warehouse load run log and the data catalog entry for the engagement tables.

steps.title: Define the source objects and incremental watermark
sop: List the source objects: sends, opens, clicks, form submissions and unsubscribes.
Choose the incremental watermark column for each object.
Record the object and watermark mapping in the pipeline config.
Done when every object has a watermark column defined.
verify: Read the pipeline config for objects without a watermark.
Pass when every configured object has an incremental watermark.

steps.title: Configure the load to be idempotent on re-run
sop: Set the load to merge on the natural event key rather than insert.
Define the event key covering contact, event type and event timestamp.
Document the merge behaviour in the pipeline config.
Done when the load uses a merge on the defined event key.
verify: Re-run the same window through the pipeline deliberately.
Pass when no duplicate engagement rows exist after the re-run.

steps.title: Schedule the load and reconcile the test window
sop: Set the load schedule and its dependency order.
Run the pipeline for the agreed test window.
Compare landing table counts to the platform API counts.
Done when the test window is loaded and counts compared.
verify: Check the count comparison for each source object.
Pass when landing counts reconcile to the platform API counts.

steps.title: Register the ingested tables in the data catalog
sop: Create catalog entries for each ingested engagement table.
Record owner, classification and refresh frequency on each entry.
Link the entries to the upstream marketing platform source.
Done when every ingested table has a complete catalog entry.
verify: List ingested tables with no catalog entry or missing fields.
Pass when every ingested table is registered with owner and classification.

steps.title: Enable failure and late-arrival alerting
sop: Configure a failure alert on the ingestion job to the analytics list.
Configure a late-arrival alert against the expected arrival time.
Trigger a test alert and confirm receipt.
Done when both alerts are active and tested.
verify: Check the analytics inbox for the test alert.
Pass when the test alert was received naming the failing job.

steps.title: Validate engagement data usability with the campaign team
sop: Query the ingested tables for a recent campaign.
Confirm sends, opens, clicks and unsubscribes are present and joinable.
Report any missing event type to the pipeline owner.
Done when the campaign query returns all expected event types.
verify: Compare the queried event counts to the platform campaign report.
Pass when queried counts match the platform campaign report.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every marketing extract and published report leaving the warehouse or BI platform.
generic.In-scope period: The current control review cycle covering live outputs.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each output records classification, masking rule, cohort minimum and permitted use.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Reviewed output count matches the catalog list of published marketing outputs.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Access log review and masking test results stored with their review dates.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Access outside the approved group is logged and challenged with an outcome.
generic.Test population: All published marketing reports and restricted extracts in the period.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Zero published reports expose unmasked direct identifiers.
generic.Exception handling path: An unmasked identifier found forces the output offline until corrected.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Every access to a restricted marketing extract is attributable to a named user.
generic.Evidence location: Data catalog classification records and the BI platform access log.

steps.title: Classify every marketing extract and report in the catalog
sop: List published marketing extracts and reports from the catalog.
Assign or confirm the classification on each output.
Record the restricted fields present in each output.
Done when every output carries a classification.
verify: List outputs with a blank classification.
Pass when every marketing output has an assigned classification.

steps.title: Apply masking or tokenisation to restricted fields
sop: Configure masking or tokenisation for each restricted field in the output layer.
Rebuild the affected extracts and reports.
Record the masking rule applied per field.
Done when every restricted field is masked or tokenised.
verify: Inspect a sampled report for full policy number, national id or full date of birth.
Pass when no published report exposes unmasked direct identifiers.

steps.title: Enforce the minimum cohort size on aggregate outputs
sop: Apply the minimum cohort size rule to aggregate marketing outputs.
Suppress or combine cells falling below the minimum.
Record the cohort threshold used on each output.
Done when every aggregate output enforces the cohort minimum.
verify: Query the published aggregates for cells below the minimum.
Pass when no aggregate cell falls below the minimum cohort size.

steps.title: Attach use-limitation notices to external agency outputs
sop: Identify outputs shared with external agencies.
Attach the agreed use-limitation notice and the expiry date.
Confirm the receiving agreement covers the shared data.
Done when every external output carries a notice and expiry.
verify: Open a sampled external output.
Pass when the notice and expiry date are present on the output.

steps.title: Review the access log for restricted marketing outputs
